context.exploration_scope: Finalized the Principle's application boundary using S7's real PRINCIPLE_MISMATCH finding: stated the application/non-application conditions explicitly, then validated the unmodified boundary rule against a third real, previously-untested case

problem: PHASE-SSI-S7 showed the Principle correctly refuses to apply to one different real case, but a boundary demonstrated on exactly one counter-example is not yet a stated, checkable rule -- and had not been tested against any further real case to see whether it generalizes correctly rather than having been tuned to that single example.

decision.decision_summary: Boundary rule (reused verbatim from S7, not modified): applies only when chain_status=BLOCKED AND owner_domain matches an infrastructure keyword AND action_type="infra_restoration". Tested against all 3 real cases: goal_production_runtime(applies=true,expected=true,correct=true), goal_semantic_quality(applies=false,expected=false,correct=true), goal_ghibli_production_pipeline(applies=false,expected=false,correct=true). All correct: true. Principle's own content: unmodified. 0 CI wiring, 0 automatic policy, 0 automatic execution, 0 real project modifications. Verdict: PRINCIPLE_BOUNDARY_VALIDATED.

action.action_summary: Re-confirmed the 2 existing real cases, stated the application/non-application boundary explicitly as the same mechanical rule S7 already used, and tested that unmodified rule against a third real, previously-untested chain (goal_ghibli_production_pipeline, status=RESOLVED) to confirm it classifies correctly without needing adjustment.

result.note: The same unmodified boundary rule correctly classified all 3 real cases (1 where the Principle applies, 2 where it correctly does not, for two different real reasons) -- the boundary is now a stated, checkable rule, not just a single counter-example.

cause.root_cause_summary: A rule inferred from a single counter-example (S7) risks being an ad hoc description of that one case rather than a real boundary -- it only becomes trustworthy once it is stated explicitly and then checked, unmodified, against further real data it was not built from.

lesson: Validating a boundary means writing the rule down before testing it further, then running it -- unchanged -- against a real case that had no part in deriving it; if the rule needs adjusting to fit the new case, it was never a boundary, only a description of the one example that produced it.
